issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat): the template's example usage in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java shows commented example calls using two constructor arguments (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem statement UML and the reference solution define Animal and its subclasses with a single-argument constructor that accepts only the name (e.g., public Animal(String name) and public Seal(String name)). This inconsistency can mislead students about the required constructor signatures and cause them to implement constructors that do not match the intended design or the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the example code in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java in the template to use single-argument constructors matching the UML and solution (e.g., Seal seal = new Seal("Clarabelle"); Pig pig = new Pig("Doodle"); Goat goat = new Goat("Buttinsky");). Alternatively, if a second attribute (e.g., type/habitat) was intended pedagogically, update the problem_statement.md UML and the solution implementation to add and initialize that second attribute in Animal and all subclasses, and adjust all constructors and documentation accordingly.
